commentary_segments.text: By use of the coefficients d, the distortion components IM and IM with feed- 2f 3f back (index f ) are easily calculated. The IM contains T2 in 2f the denominator. If we associate one T to the reduction of the gain, and as a consequence, the reduction of the relative current swing, then we see that the IM is 2f reduced by T itself. A rule of thumb is that we calculate the distortion for the relative current swing, taking into account the effect of the feedback on this current swing. The distortion for this stage is now easily calculated. It is divided by the loop gain to take into account the reduction by the loop gain T. In the same way, IM is calculated. Again, the two terms appear related to a and a . If a is 3f 3 2 3 dominant, the same rule of thumb applies. An easy way to calculate the distortion is to find the distortion for a relative current swing, taking into account the effect of feedback. The distortion is then obtained by division by the loop gain T itself, and not by T2. The same is true if a is dominant. Indeed the T2 in the denominator is reduced to T since 2 the numerator also contains T. Clearly, we have assumed all along that T is always larger than unity and that the loop gain can be represented by T, rather than 1+T.

analysis_objective_excerpts.text: By use of the coefficients d, the distortion components IM and IM with feed- 2f 3f back (index f ) are easily calculated.
A rule of thumb is that we calculate the distortion for the relative current swing, taking into account the effect of the feedback on this current swing.
The distortion for this stage is now easily calculated.

source_conclusions.text: If we associate one T to the reduction of the gain, and as a consequence, the reduction of the relative current swing, then we see that the IM is 2f reduced by T itself.
It is divided by the loop gain to take into account the reduction by the loop gain T.
The distortion is then obtained by division by the loop gain T itself, and not by T2.
Clearly, we have assumed all along that T is always larger than unity and that the loop gain can be represented by T, rather than 1+T.
